recovered_habits.boundary_condition: If inventory is at risk, only hold cancellable rooms or fare holds while waiting for the missing details.
recovered_habits.default_action: Draft a non-booking plan, ask the client for the missing operational details, then route one approval-ready package with open items called out.

evidence.quote: Let’s not book until I get the address and Friday timing. What should I ask the client?
Okay. Don’t book anything yet. Just give me the skeleton I can paste into my notes.
I don’t want to overbuild this before the client confirms. What should I ask them?
Great. Give me a tentative plan I can share internally, but mark it as not ready to book.
For approval I need a shortlist, not final booking. Keep the hotel well-rated—around 4.0 or better from guests if possible. Breakfast is helpful but not the deciding factor.

recovered_habits.exception_condition: Proceed to booking once manager approval is in and the unresolved items no longer affect the flight, hotel area, or transport choice.
recovered_habits.name: Hold work bookings until site and agenda details are firm
recovered_habits.preference_value: Work trips should stay provisional until the exact client or organizer site, first required onsite time, return-day end time, and local transport assumptions are known.
recovered_habits.scope_condition: Solo work/client/conference trips where the address, Monday requirement, Thursday wrap, or transport plan is still uncertain.

recovered_habits.boundary_condition: A one-stop can be considered if the fare gap is large, the layover is comfortable and short, and the timing still protects the trip purpose.
recovered_habits.default_action: Search nonstop options first and reject small-savings connections, long layovers, or fussy routings.

evidence.quote: Keep the flights simple: nonstop if it is not a silly price, otherwise one short layover.
I’d rather not deal with a fussy connection for such a short trip.
I would rather not connect for a trip this short unless the savings are huge.
I would rather keep it nonstop if the price difference is small. I don't need to save $70 and add a connection.
Use the $300 nightly cap as pre-tax. If Delta has a comparable nonstop, include it, but schedule matters more. I do not want a one-stop unless it saves a lot.

recovered_habits.exception_condition: If nonstops are unavailable, badly timed, or at a clearly unreasonable premium, use the simplest one-stop backup.
recovered_habits.name: Prefer nonstop or very simple routings
recovered_habits.preference_value: Nonstop flights are the default; a one-stop is acceptable only when the nonstop is oddly priced, badly timed, or the savings are substantial.
recovered_habits.scope_condition: Flights from Atlanta for work and family trips, especially short trips where a connection can consume much of the travel day.

recovered_habits.boundary_condition: Do not pay a large premium or accept a worse day just to fly Delta.
recovered_habits.default_action: Include Delta in the comparison and select it when the schedule and total price are comparable.

evidence.quote: From ATL, Delta is nice if comparable, but I’m fine with another carrier.
Use Delta if the 5:40-ish outbound and Tuesday afternoon return are still close to American.
Can you include Delta if it’s close, but don’t force it if another nonstop is much cheaper?
That sounds right. Delta is fine if the schedule is sensible, but I don’t need to force it. No long layovers for this.
For MSP I would prefer a nonstop if the timing is decent. Delta is fine if it is not absurd.
For now, assume ATL to MSP, economy, Monday to Thursday. If a Delta nonstop is close on price, include it, but don't force it.

recovered_habits.exception_condition: Choose another carrier when it is meaningfully cheaper, has better times, or better family seat availability.
recovered_habits.name: Use Delta as a tie-breaker, not a mandate
recovered_habits.preference_value: Delta is preferred when price and timing are close, but carrier preference should not override a materially better schedule or fare on another airline.
recovered_habits.scope_condition: Atlanta-origin itineraries where Delta and another nonstop carrier are both available.

recovered_habits.boundary_condition: Avoid unnecessarily early flights when Monday is remote or optional, but still protect any afternoon kickoff or evening event.
recovered_habits.default_action: Pick a Monday or day-before outbound that lands by early afternoon or dinner, rather than the cheapest late arrival.

evidence.quote: I’d like to land Monday with time to check in and eat before Tuesday morning meetings.
I’d rather arrive Monday early enough to review materials, not at 10 p.m.
I don’t want to land at MSP after nine and then have to be sharp Tuesday morning.
I agree. I don’t want to start a client week tired because of a connection.
Exactly. I want a prep block Monday afternoon.
Will the Monday morning flight still leave time for the reception if I cannot check in early?

recovered_habits.exception_condition: Use Sunday evening or an earlier Monday flight only if Monday morning onsite attendance is required or the normal outbound would risk a fixed kickoff.
recovered_habits.name: Arrive for work trips with prep, check-in, and dinner buffer
recovered_habits.preference_value: For work trips, avoid late arrivals before early client days; arrive with enough time to check in, eat, review materials, and handle prep.
recovered_habits.scope_condition: Work trips where the first onsite session is the next morning or a same-day kickoff/reception may occur.

recovered_habits.boundary_condition: An earlier return is acceptable only when the client gives a firm early end time and the airport transfer is clearly safe.
recovered_habits.default_action: Use a return time with enough buffer for meeting overrun, bag pickup, ground transfer, and security, even if it gets home later.

evidence.quote: I’d rather get home earlier if it’s not reckless. I just don’t want to create a change fee problem.
Okay, change the return to the evening nonstop. I need a quick explanation for the fare difference.
The Minneapolis training team just added an optional Thursday lab from 1:00 to 3:30. My return draft is still the 3:45 p.m. nonstop, which now feels too tight.
Thursday return should not make me bolt out of the room. I hate leaving a client session half-packed.
No thanks. Is there a later nonstop?
Can you make Friday morning a backup in the note but still recommend Thursday?

recovered_habits.exception_condition: If the end time moves later or becomes uncertain, change only the return leg when possible rather than adding a connection or rushing the client day.
recovered_habits.name: Protect client closeouts with return-flight buffer
recovered_habits.preference_value: Do not choose a return flight that requires sprinting out of a client session; move to a later nonstop when the closeout, lab, or debrief may run long.
recovered_habits.scope_condition: Work-trip return days after client closeouts, steering committees, labs, or conference closing sessions.

recovered_habits.boundary_condition: Main Cabin does not need to be fully refundable; the key is seat selection and usable change rules.
recovered_habits.default_action: Book Main Cabin/economy standard fares and do not prepay extras unless needed.

evidence.quote: Okay. Main Cabin, not Basic. For seats, three together if possible, but if not, one adult next to our child matters more than all three being in the same row.
Go ahead with those. Main Cabin, not Basic.
What about fare type? I don’t want to accidentally lose the seat assignments.
Yes: main cabin, no checked bag for now. Put me at the window and keep Leela and Ravi with me if possible.
Correct on main cabin and no checked bag. Take the rear window seats. I'd rather have the window than a forward aisle for this one.
Correct. Main Cabin, carry-on only, work card. Please get a window seat even if it’s behind the wing.

recovered_habits.exception_condition: Basic Economy is not used in recurring examples where seating or flexibility matters; consider only if seat placement is irrelevant and savings are compelling.
recovered_habits.name: Avoid Basic Economy when seat control or flexibility matters
recovered_habits.preference_value: Use Main Cabin or equivalent standard economy rather than Basic Economy when advance seat selection, family seating, or work-trip change flexibility matters.
recovered_habits.scope_condition: Family trips and work trips where assigned seats, changes, or schedule stability are important.

recovered_habits.boundary_condition: Avoid last-row or poor seats when possible, and do not pay preferred-seat fees just to move a few rows.
recovered_habits.default_action: Select adjacent seats first; take a window within that arrangement when available; for solo flights choose a no-fee window over a forward aisle or middle.

evidence.quote: For seats, three together if possible, but if not, one adult next to our child matters more than all three being in the same row.
Seats matter more with the kid. Can you keep us together, and if there’s a window for me, use it?
Put Nia by the window outbound. For the return I’ll take the window unless she insists. Main thing is not splitting us up.
Seats next. I want our child between us or right next to both of us. If I can get the window, great, but together matters more.
Seat maps show a few windows toward the back. Forward seats are mostly aisle or middle. I’d rather take a window than a forward aisle, as long as it is not the last row.
Take the rear windows. A forward middle is not worth it. Also add a quiet-room request at the hotel if there is a field for it.

recovered_habits.exception_condition: If a full family row is unavailable, use a child-plus-adult pair with the other adult across the aisle or nearby.
recovered_habits.name: Seat selection prioritizes togetherness, then no-fee windows
recovered_habits.preference_value: For family trips, keep the group together and ensure the child is next to an adult; for solo/work flights, take a no-fee window even if farther back, but do not pay or split the group just for seat location.
recovered_habits.scope_condition: Seat assignment on booked flights for both family and solo work travel.

recovered_habits.boundary_condition: Anything below roughly 4.0 needs a clearly stated reason and tradeoff.
recovered_habits.default_action: Filter to well-reviewed properties first, then compare location, breakfast, dinner, room setup, and cancellation terms.

evidence.quote: For the hotel, I’d like a solid guest rating, around 4.0 or better, breakfast if practical, and easy dinner nearby.
For reviews, don't include anything under about 4.0 unless there's a very good reason.
Keep the review quality in the mix too. I don’t want a beach motel that is only winning because it’s close.
Can you do a first-pass shortlist by type, keeping it around 4-star guest reviews or better but not luxury?
Please don't include anything with weak reviews. Four stars or better if possible.
And please don’t send me anything with weak reviews just because it’s cheaper.

recovered_habits.exception_condition: If the destination has very limited options, flag the quality issue rather than hiding it in a cheap recommendation.
recovered_habits.name: Use a strong guest-review floor for hotels
recovered_habits.preference_value: Hotels should generally have solid guest reviews around 4.0+; do not accept weak, sketchy, noisy, or poorly reviewed lodging just to save money.
recovered_habits.scope_condition: Hotel shortlists for work and family trips.

recovered_habits.boundary_condition: Use breakfast as a tie-breaker among otherwise comparable hotels.
recovered_habits.default_action: Choose the better-located or better-room hotel when breakfast is the only major drawback, and plan paid hotel breakfast, cafes, grab-and-go, or groceries instead.

evidence.quote: Breakfast would simplify mornings, but I wouldn’t pick a bad location just to get free waffles.
What about hotels? Breakfast is useful, but not if I’m signing up for a bad commute every morning.
Breakfast included would be nice, but I don’t want to choose a worse location just for that.
Breakfast included would help, but not if it means the room is a shoebox.
I like included breakfast, but I don't want to make both mornings harder for this trip.
I do not care if breakfast is paid if the mornings are easier. Is the campus property under $250 before tax and cancellable?

recovered_habits.exception_condition: A breakfast-included hotel can lead if it also preserves commute, room quality, and reviews; otherwise it remains the backup.
recovered_habits.name: Treat included breakfast as a plus, not the deciding factor
recovered_habits.preference_value: Included breakfast is useful, especially with early starts or a child, but it should not outweigh a better location, safer commute, larger room, or quieter stay.
recovered_habits.scope_condition: Hotel comparisons where one option includes breakfast and another has better logistics or room quality.

recovered_habits.boundary_condition: A less convenient dinner situation is acceptable only when the location or room setup clearly wins and rideshares are easy.
recovered_habits.default_action: Prefer hotels near restaurants or with an on-site restaurant/bar, even if breakfast is paid or room rate is slightly higher.

evidence.quote: Hotel-wise, I need good reviews, breakfast if possible, and somewhere I can get dinner without a whole production after long days.
Then I don’t want that as first choice. I don’t want to be hunting for dinner after 7.
For the hotel, I want strong guest ratings, short rideshares, breakfast if it’s practical, and somewhere to eat dinner nearby. I won’t have a car.
I want simple flights into Tampa or Sarasota, a Sunday return that doesn't wreck Monday, and a hotel or condo setup where beach, pool, breakfast or groceries, and casual dinners are easy with a kid.
I will not have a car, so dinner nearby matters if we land late or I am done late.
Please include breakfast and dinner access when you compare later, but I agree area is first.

recovered_habits.exception_condition: For beach or family stays, groceries/cafes can solve breakfast, but casual dinner nearby remains important.
recovered_habits.name: Require easy dinner access at hotels
recovered_habits.preference_value: Hotels should have on-site dining or easy nearby casual dinner options so evenings after work, flights, or family activities are not a production.
recovered_habits.scope_condition: Hotel selection for no-car work trips, family weekends, beach stays, and late-arrival days.

recovered_habits.boundary_condition: A slightly higher refundable rate is acceptable for flexibility.
recovered_habits.default_action: Book or hold cancellable rates, verify cancellation cutoff, and keep backup options only until the preferred reservation is safe.

evidence.quote: Denver can be cancellable. Estes is where I need answers before paying anything nonrefundable.
Should I book both Estes places cancellable while I ask questions?
Which pieces should I put on a cancellable hold tonight?
Hotel rates moved though. The Study is now $279 refundable, and Homewood is $206 but prepaid with several new elevator complaints. Would you still book The Study?
So final pick is the Thursday nonstop, Sunday midafternoon nonstop, and River Walk refundable room?
If the official hotel stays cancellable through that deadline, I think that is the cleanest.

recovered_habits.exception_condition: A prepaid rate may be considered only when trip risk is low and the savings are meaningful, but recent behavior favors cancellable options even at a higher rate.
recovered_habits.name: Prefer cancellable hotel bookings and avoid prepaid rates while plans can change
recovered_habits.preference_value: Hotel bookings should usually be refundable/cancellable, with cancellation deadlines tracked; prepaid or nonrefundable rates are avoided unless plans are very firm and savings justify the risk.
recovered_habits.scope_condition: Work and family hotel reservations, especially before schedules, PTO, client agendas, or weather-sensitive plans are fully stable.

recovered_habits.boundary_condition: Treat these as requests, not guarantees; do not change otherwise good hotels solely because the request cannot be guaranteed.
recovered_habits.default_action: Add quiet-room and away-from-elevator requests at booking, and repeat or confirm them at check-in when relevant.

evidence.quote: Please note no rental car and request a quiet room away from the elevator.
Yes, standard king. Please ask for a quiet room away from elevators and not facing the main street if that is an option.
Please add hotel requests: high floor, away from elevators, quiet room, king if available, and luggage hold Thursday.
Hotel requests: away from elevator noise, and not a low floor if possible. Should I add early check-in?
Can you add a quiet room request away from elevators and make sure the no-car plan is in the notes?
Please also add a quiet-room request for the hotel, away from elevators if possible.

recovered_habits.exception_condition: High-floor requests can be omitted when the important part is simply avoiding elevator/noise exposure.
recovered_habits.name: Add quiet-room hotel requests by default
recovered_habits.preference_value: Ask hotels for a quiet room, usually away from elevators, ice machines, and street/noise sources; high floor is often preferred when available.
recovered_habits.scope_condition: Hotel bookings for work and family trips where notes or special requests can be added.

recovered_habits.boundary_condition: For suburban sites, multi-site days, road-closure/parking uncertainty, grocery needs, or inland beach lodging, compare a cancellable/pay-later rental.
recovered_habits.default_action: Plan no rental car, choose hotel locations that make rideshare/transit practical, and add rideshare notes for reimbursement.

evidence.quote: No rental car unless the office location makes that impractical.
For the hotel, I want strong guest ratings, short rideshares, breakfast if it’s practical, and somewhere to eat dinner nearby. I won’t have a car.
I would rather not rent a car if rideshare or transit is workable.
Hotel ceiling is $250 before tax, and no rental car.
No rental car. Add simple rideshare notes for the airport, hotel, and office so reimbursement has the rationale.
Put A Line as preferred, rideshare if weather is bad or the train is delayed.

recovered_habits.exception_condition: Add a rental only when the location, parking, offsite movement, or family logistics make rideshare/transit impractical.
recovered_habits.name: Avoid rental cars when rideshare or transit is workable
recovered_habits.preference_value: Do not rent a car by default; use rideshare, walking, transit, or airport rail when a fixed urban site or walkable stay makes that workable.
recovered_habits.scope_condition: Solo work trips to urban campuses/downtowns and family city trips with no-car itineraries.

recovered_habits.boundary_condition: A remote airport becomes viable when it saves several hundred dollars total and does not create a late or complicated arrival.
recovered_habits.default_action: Benchmark the most convenient airport and central neighborhood first, then price remote airports only as savings checks.

evidence.quote: DCA seems easiest, but I'm open to IAD or BWI if the fare difference is real.
That's my worry with Newark. If it saves enough, fine, but I do not want the first night to become a project.
If DCA is only $100 or $150 more total, I don’t want to drag everyone through a longer transfer. If BWI saves $400 or more, I’d consider it.
Yes, I wondered about Providence. If BOS is way more, maybe, but I don't want a whole extra logistics project.
My spouse says simplest city access matters more than squeezing out the lowest fare, as long as the difference is not ridiculous.

recovered_habits.exception_condition: If the convenient airport fare spikes sharply or seats/schedule are poor, recompare remote airport plus ground transfer before booking.
recovered_habits.name: For short family city trips, pay a reasonable premium for easier city access
recovered_habits.preference_value: For museum/city weekends with a child, choose the closest/practical airport and central hotel access when the fare difference is modest; remote airports are considered only for large total savings.
recovered_habits.scope_condition: Short family city trips from Atlanta, especially Washington, New York, and Boston where ground transfer time can dominate the first or last day.

recovered_habits.boundary_condition: Two doubles can be tolerated for a short two-night stay if ratings, location, breakfast, and cancellation are strong.
recovered_habits.default_action: Book a family-suitable room type, verify bed setup, and favor larger rooms for longer stays.

evidence.quote: Hotels: near Metro, room for three, not fancy, but not sketchy.
One room is fine, preferably two queens but a king plus sofa would work if the room is bigger.
Are the small rooms going to make us regret it?
For hotels, I care about easy museum access and casual dinner nearby. I don’t want a tiny room if we do four nights. Breakfast would be nice, but not if the room is miserable.
Two queens first. King plus a real sofa bed is okay. And please don’t send me anything with weak reviews just because it’s cheaper.

recovered_habits.exception_condition: Do not accept one bed plus uncertain rollaway/sofa arrangements unless the hotel confirms the setup.
recovered_habits.name: Family hotel rooms must genuinely work for three
recovered_habits.preference_value: For family stays, room setup and breathing room matter: two queens are preferred; a king plus a real sofa bed can work; tiny or uncertain rooms are avoided even if breakfast is included.
recovered_habits.scope_condition: Family hotel selection for city, museum, and long-weekend trips with two adults and a child.

recovered_habits.boundary_condition: Resort fees and paid breakfast must be visible before booking, and the family room/mini-fridge setup should be verified.
recovered_habits.default_action: Choose Gulf-side or beach-block lodging with pool and nearby casual food, then solve breakfast with groceries, cafes, or selective paid breakfast.

evidence.quote: Two adults and one child. Beach access matters more than fancy, but I don’t want every day to depend on a car. Pool would help. Breakfast would simplify mornings, but I wouldn’t pick a bad location just to get free waffles.
We are not planning excursions. Maybe one dinner away from the beach, but otherwise I’d rather not manage rental counters, parking, and a booster seat.
For lodging, I don't want us loading the car just to touch the beach every day.
We talked it over. For St. Pete, Gulf-side beats the bigger inland suite. Can you help me move this from comparison to booking before that cancellable family room disappears?

recovered_habits.exception_condition: Use an inland suite or add a pay-later rental only if the beach property fails room/fee checks, savings are large, or weather/grocery/off-beach plans make a car worthwhile.
recovered_habits.name: For short beach trips, favor walkable Gulf-side lodging over inland savings
recovered_habits.preference_value: For beach weekends with a child, walkable beach/pool/dinner convenience beats a bigger or cheaper inland suite with breakfast.
recovered_habits.scope_condition: Short Gulf Coast or beach-oriented family trips where beach time is the main goal.

recovered_habits.boundary_condition: Keep the note concise when the manager asks for brevity, but still include the operational reason for higher cost.
recovered_habits.default_action: Provide a pasteable recommendation with cost, schedule rationale, comparison against cheaper flights/hotels, and open items.

evidence.quote: Can you make the approval note include why I’m not choosing the cheaper one-stop?
What are the realistic alternates? I need the change cost visible for approval.
Add the unresolved items so procurement doesn’t think I ignored them.
Please write the package summary for approval. Include the tradeoffs and any missing confirmations.
Add the reason for not choosing the one-stop fares.
Good. Give me the final package I can forward. Do not book yet.

recovered_habits.exception_condition: After final approval and booking, switch to concise checklist/receipt notes rather than re-litigating all alternatives.
recovered_habits.name: Approval notes should justify tradeoffs and rejected cheaper options
recovered_habits.preference_value: Approval or manager notes should explicitly show the recommended choice, why cheaper alternatives were rejected, any change cost, and unresolved items.
recovered_habits.scope_condition: Work-trip approvals, travel changes, and procurement-facing recommendations.
